src: U.P.P.C.S. (Mains) 2003
s:
Given below are two statements. One is labelled as Assertion and other as
Reason :
Assertion (A) : The frequency of landslides has increased in the Himalayas.
Reason (R) : There has been large scale mining in the Himalayas in recent years. In the context of the above which one of the following is correct :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct
x: The frequency of landslides has increased in the Himalayas. Its root cause is the increased frequency of earthquakes as well as manual activities such as the construction of roads and dams. There has been large scale mining done for the construction of roads, dams, and minerals in the Himalayas in recent years. That is why the frequency of landslides has increased in the Himalayas. Thus, both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

s: Which of the following was the capital of Andhra State when it was made a separate state in the year 1953?
x: In an effort to gain a separate state based on linguistic grounds, Potti Shriramulu fasted until death in 1952. After Shriramulu's death, the Telugu speaking areas of Andhra state were carved out of Madras state in October, 1953 with Kurnool as its capital city. Later in 1956, Hyderabad was made the capital of Andhra Pradesh. Andhra Pradesh was bifurcated in 2014 and a separate state of Telangana was formed. However, in accordance with the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014 Hyderabad will remain the de jure capital of both Andhra Pradesh and Telangana for a period not exceeding 10 years. src: UPSC CSE Prelims 2005
s: Which one of the following is the correct sequence of the given hills starting from the north and going towards the south?
o: Nallamalai Hills – Nilgiri Hills – Javadi Hills – Anaimalai Hills
Anaimalai Hills – Javadi Hills – Nilgiri Hills – Nallamalai Hills
Nallamalai Hills – Javadi Hills – Nilgiri Hills – Anaimalai Hills
Anaimalai Hills – Nilgiri Hills – Javadi Hills – Nallamalai Hills
x: The Nallamala Hills, located in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, form part of the Eastern Ghats and are the northernmost among the given hills. South of them lie the Javadi Hills, an Eastern Ghats range in northern Tamil Nadu. Further south are the Nilgiri Hills, situated at the junction of the Eastern and Western Ghats. Beyond the Nilgiris, and south of the Palghat Gap, are the Anaimalai Hills of the Western Ghats, making them the southernmost in the list.

src: I.A.S. (Pre) 2007
s: Where are Shevaroy Hills located ?
x: Shevaroy Hills are located in the Salem district in Tamil Nadu. The height of Shevaroy Hills is about 4000 to 5000 feet above sea level. Its total covering area is about 50 sq. km. The famous 'Yercaud' hill station is situated in these hills.

src: I.A.S. (Pre) 2005
s: Which one of the following is the correct sequence of the given hills starting from the north and going towards the south?
o: Nallamalai Hills – Nilgiri Hills – Javadi Hills –
Anaimalai Hills – Nilgiri Hills – Javadi Hills –
x: Nallamalai Hills are situated between the Krishna River and Pennar River, stretched from north to south, parallel to the Coromandel Coast on the Bay of Bengal. Javadi Hills are located on the Eastern Ghats in the Vellore and Tiruvannamalai districts of Tamil Nadu State. Renowned as the ‘Blue Mountains’, Nilgiri Hills are located at the junction of Western Ghats and Eastern Ghats. Doddabetta is the highest peak in the Nilgiri Hills at 2,637 metres. The Anaimalai or Anamalai Hills form the southern portion of the Western Ghats and span up to the border of Kerala and Tamil Nadu in southern India. Anaimudi is the highest peak in the Anaimalai Hills at 2695 metres. These four hills are located in Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu and Kerala states in India from north to south. Hence, the correct option is (c).
